text: Explain how precedent works in the English legal system. Discuss the strengths and weaknesses
of this source of law. [25]
‘We believe that 12 persons, selected at random … represent the views of the common man …’
– Lord Denning.
Explain the selection process for jurors. Assess the validity of Lord Denning’s view. [25]
Describe the process by which an idea for a change in the law becomes an Act of Parliament.
Discuss the main criticisms of the legislative process. [25]
Explain the appeal routes in civil cases. Analyse the difficulties that an individual might face in
pursuing such an appeal. [25]
‘Their ignorance of whole areas of British life is shattering. They receive no training whatever …’
– Lord Gifford.
Describe how judges are recruited and trained. Assess the extent to which the statement above is
true. [25]
Explain the current law on stop and search. Assess the extent to which suspects are adequately
protected by this law. [25]
